user_stories.story: As a user, when I create a rule for a symbol no browser is watching, the backend still receives that symbol's prices so the rule can fire.
As a user, symbols with rules stay subscribed upstream across backend restarts and across browser connect/disconnect.
As a user, when a rule fires I can see it afterwards: GET /api/alerts and a dashboard Alerts section with a Refresh button.
As a user, alerts remain visible after I delete the rule that produced them.

As an operator, the number of watched symbols is capped (WATCHLIST_MAX_SYMBOLS, default 50) so the free Finnhub tier is not exceeded; a rule for a new symbol beyond the cap is rejected with 409 and nothing is saved.

As a maintainer, dead code X1 (Services._spawn, _tasks), X2 (ConnectionManager.broadcast, broadcast_symbol, and connection_ids if unused afterwards) and X4 (RuleStore.add) is gone with no behaviour change.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: At startup (CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS) the DB has watchlist(symbol TEXT PRIMARY KEY, created_at DOUBLE PRECISION NOT NULL) and alerts(id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, rule_id TEXT NOT NULL, symbol TEXT NOT NULL, rule_type TEXT NOT NULL, threshold DOUBLE PRECISION NOT NULL, price DOUBLE PRECISION NOT NULL, triggered_at DOUBLE PRECISION NOT NULL), plus an index on alerts(triggered_at DESC). alerts has NO foreign key to alert_rules. Pass: real-PG test inspects information_schema/pg_constraint and finds the tables, the index and no FK; running startup twice does not error.

config.py has watchlist_max_symbols: int = 50 (env WATCHLIST_MAX_SYMBOLS) and .env.example documents it. Pass: Settings(_env_file=None).watchlist_max_symbols == 50; env override works; .env.example contains WATCHLIST_MAX_SYMBOLS.

POST /api/rules for a new symbol returns 201, and in one DB transaction: cap check, INSERT watchlist (ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING), INSERT alert_rules. Pass (fast): fake DB holds the rule and the watchlist row. Pass (real PG): if the rule INSERT fails (e.g. duplicate id forced), no watchlist row remains for that symbol.

Cap: with N = cap distinct watched symbols, POST /api/rules for an (N+1)th NEW symbol returns 409 and no rule and no watchlist row is saved, the in-memory rule store/watchlist are unchanged, and no upstream subscribe is sent. A rule for an already-watched symbol at the cap still returns 201. Pass (fast): small cap in test Settings (e.g. 2). Pass (real PG): same, plus the check is race-safe (the transaction takes a lock, e.g. advisory lock or table lock, so concurrent creations of different new symbols at cap-1 cannot both succeed; test fires two concurrent POSTs and asserts exactly one 201 and one 409).

DB failure on POST /api/rules returns 503 with the existing generic body ("rule storage unavailable") and changes nothing in memory (no rule in RuleStore, symbol not added to watchlist, no subscribe). Error handling pattern in routers/rules.py is otherwise unchanged (409 is an added, distinct case; 503 detail must not leak connection info).

After a successful POST for a newly watched symbol with no browser holding it, the upstream fake receives exactly 1 subscribe call for that symbol. A second rule on the same symbol: 0 further subscribes. If a browser already holds the symbol upstream (ref_count > 0), the rule path sends 0 subscribes. If the upstream subscribe raises, POST still returns 201 and the failure is logged (no exception propagates).

Upstream symbol set == watchlist UNION browser-subscribed symbols, with no duplicate subscribe and no wrong unsubscribe: (a) browser subscribes to a watched symbol: 0 upstream subscribes; (b) browser subscribes to an unwatched symbol: 1 subscribe, and when the last browser leaves (or disconnects) 1 unsubscribe; (c) the last browser leaving a watched symbol sends 0 unsubscribes; (d) a rule created on a symbol a browser holds sends 0 subscribes, and afterwards that browser leaving sends 0 unsubscribes; (e) two browsers on a watched symbol: no subscribe/unsubscribe traffic at all. The decision must be correct under interleaving: SubscriptionManager calls upstream while holding its lock and awaiting, while the rule path runs in other request tasks, so the watchlist update and the "does a browser hold it" check on the rule path must be made without an await between them, and the browser path's upstream callback must still send exactly one subscribe overall when a rule and a first browser race for the same symbol (never zero, never two). Pass: unit tests over Services with FakeFinnhubClient recording subscribe/unsubscribe call lists, including a deterministic interleaving test (browser subscribe suspended inside the upstream call while a rule is created).

The get_symbols callable passed to the upstream factory returns the sorted union of watchlist and browser-subscribed symbols (each once), evaluated at every (re)connect. Pass: with watchlist {A,B} and browser holding {B,C}, get_symbols() == [A,B,C]; the fake client's connect sends exactly one subscribe per symbol of the union. SubscriptionManager.active_symbols itself may stay browser-only, the union lives in the Services-provided callable.

At startup the watchlist is loaded from Postgres into memory before the upstream is started, so the first connect subscribes all watched symbols. Pass (real PG): create a rule via app 1, shut down, start app 2 on the same DB: the fake upstream's initial symbol set includes the symbol. If the DB is unavailable at startup the watchlist is empty, the app starts, /health returns 200, and ticks still flow.

Pre-existing rules (alert_rules rows whose symbol has no watchlist row, created before this feature) get their symbols added to the watchlist at startup (idempotent backfill, cap not applied), so L1 is fixed for existing data. Pass (real PG): insert an alert_rules row directly, start the app, symbol is in the watchlist and subscribed.

Services.on_tick: for every (rule, event) fired by the engine, one alert (new id, rule_id, symbol, rule_type, threshold, price, triggered_at from the event) is enqueued via a non-blocking, synchronous enqueue; the INFO "rule fired" log line is kept. Edge-triggered semantics preserved: a crossing tick enqueues 1; further ticks staying above enqueue 0; a tick below then above enqueues 1 more. The tick path never awaits Postgres. If the alert queue is full the alert is dropped with a warning log (no exception). If the enqueue (or the engine) raises, the websocket broadcast to subscribers still happens. Pass (fast): FakeDatabase records enqueued alerts; tests for crossing / staying above / re-arm / enqueue raising with broadcast still delivered to a subscribed fake websocket / queue-full drop (real Database with tiny queue_size and no worker consumption, or fake) / DB unavailable (pool None) enqueue is a no-op that does not raise.

A background worker (started in Database.connect, cancelled in close, independent of the ticks persistence flag) drains the alert queue in batches and INSERTs rows into alerts; an insert failure is logged by exception type only and does not kill the worker or ingestion. Pass (real PG): enqueue alerts, wait for flush (bounded poll, no fixed long sleeps), list_alerts returns them with all fields equal; after a forced insert failure a later alert is still persisted.

Deleting a rule does not delete or alter its alerts, and alerts remain listable. Pass (real PG): persist alert, DELETE /api/rules/{id}, GET /api/alerts still returns it with its stored rule_type and threshold.

GET /api/alerts?limit= returns a JSON list ordered by triggered_at DESC, id DESC; each item has id, rule_id, symbol, rule_type, threshold, price, triggered_at. Default limit 50; limit outside 1..500 (0, 501, non-integer) returns 422; DB failure or no DB returns 503 with the generic body ("alert storage unavailable" or equivalent, no exception text); same try/except + log-type-only pattern as routers/rules.py. Router registered in create_app. Pass (fast): ordering incl. ties on triggered_at broken by id DESC, limit honored, 422 cases, 503 with failing fake DB and with client_no_db.

X1: Services._spawn and Services._tasks and the shutdown loop over them are removed. X2: ConnectionManager.broadcast and broadcast_symbol removed; connection_ids removed if nothing else uses it; test_connection_manager.py adjusted so remaining behaviour (dropping failed connections via send_to, etc.) stays covered. X4: RuleStore.add removed; tests use store.put(Rule(...)) (normalising via RuleCreate/Rule). Pass: grep for "_spawn", "broadcast_symbol", "ConnectionManager.broadcast"/".broadcast(", "store.add"/"RuleStore.add" in backend/ returns nothing; the full existing suite still passes.

Every new boundary normalizes symbols with models.normalize_symbol (rule symbol already normalized by RuleCreate; any new watchlist API on db/Services and the startup backfill/load path must not store non-normalized symbols). Pass: POST with " aapl " stores AAPL in watchlist, and a browser subscribing to "aapl" is treated as watched (existing ws/symbols normalization remains).
api/client.ts exports an Alert type (id, rule_id, symbol, rule_type, threshold, price, triggered_at) and listAlerts(limit?) which GETs /api/alerts?limit= and throws on non-OK like the other helpers.

components/AlertList.tsx: loads alerts once on mount (exactly one fetch, no polling), has a Refresh button that re-fetches, shows a "last updated" time after a successful load, lists alerts in the API order (newest first) showing symbol, rule type, threshold, price and time. On fetch error it shows an error message and not an empty-list message; a subsequent successful Refresh clears the error. Empty successful result shows an explicit "no alerts" text. Dashboard.tsx renders AlertList; websocket code untouched. Pass (vitest, fetch mocked): mount calls fetch once and renders initial alert; clicking Refresh with a new alert in the mock shows it; rejected/non-OK fetch shows the error text and no "no alerts" text. Existing Dashboard test still passes (update its fetch mock if the new mount fetch requires it); npm run build and npm test pass.

pytest passes with TEST_DATABASE_URL unset (real-PG tests skipped) and with it set to an empty Postgres (real-PG tests run, 0 skipped). Real-PG tests use clean tables per test (watchlist and alerts added to the cleanup). No test hits real Finnhub.

No /api/watchlist endpoint exists after the change; no change to routers/symbols.py, routers/ws.py, useWebSocket.ts, snapshot code, latest_prices; CLAUDE.md and revised-planning.md are not edited; no git state-changing commands.

file_changes.file: Add an Alert pydantic model (response shape for GET /api/alerts; also used to carry enqueued alerts).

SCHEMA gains watchlist, alerts and the index. New: transactional create-rule-with-watchlist (raises a distinct exception, e.g. WatchlistFull, on cap; returns whether the symbol was newly added), load_watchlist, startup backfill from alert_rules, non-blocking enqueue_alert plus alert worker and queue, list_alerts(limit). Rule/alert reads and writes raise on failure (DatabaseUnavailable when pool missing); enqueue_alert is a silent no-op without a pool.

Services holds the in-memory watchlist set; remove _spawn/_tasks; upstream callbacks reconcile watchlist and browser subscriptions per AC 6-8; startup loads watchlist (failure -> empty) before starting upstream; get_symbols passed to the factory returns the union; on_tick enqueues alerts inside the existing guarded block, log line kept; include alerts router.

create_rule uses the transactional DB call; 409 on cap; 503 otherwise; after commit updates RuleStore, watchlist, and triggers the single upstream subscribe (failure logged, swallowed). Delete unchanged (symbol stays watched).
Fake gains watchlist set, create-rule-with-watchlist honoring a cap, alerts list + enqueue_alert, list_alerts, load_watchlist; honors failing flag. Optional hook to make enqueue_alert raise.

test_api_alerts.py, test_watchlist_upstream.py (or extend test_api_rules.py / test_api_symbols.py), additions to test_rules_postgres.py (or new test_alerts_postgres.py) per request; edit test_rules_engine.py and test_connection_manager.py for X2/X4; conftest client fixture may need a settings override for a small cap.

assumptions.assumption: Existing alert_rules rows predating this change are backfilled into watchlist at startup (AC 10) without applying the cap; the request did not mention migration, and without it L1 would persist for existing rules.
409 detail is a short generic message (e.g. "watchlist full"); body content is not otherwise constrained.
Cap counts distinct rows in watchlist; a rule for an already-watched symbol never trips the cap even if the table is already over cap.

The alerts worker runs whenever the DB pool exists, regardless of ticks_persistence_enabled; alerts are skipped (enqueue no-op) when there is no pool. rules_persistence_enabled=false keeps the existing behaviour of making rule/alert reads raise DatabaseUnavailable.
Alert triggered_at is the event's triggered_at (time.time() at evaluation), id is a new uuid hex per alert.

Unsubscribing a watched symbol is never done by this task (no watchlist removal path exists; D2 out of scope), so the watchlist only grows within a process; deleting rules never removes watchlist rows (decision 3).
Alert queue size is a Database constructor default (like tick queue); no new setting required.
Alerts section time formatting and "last updated" format are the implementer's choice; tests assert content, not locale format.
Alerts evicted by queue-full drop or by worker insert failure are lost (best-effort delivery), consistent with ticks; accepted per the request.

edge_cases.case: Rule created while the upstream is disconnected: subscribe is a no-op in FinnhubClient (ws None); reconnect sends the union, so the symbol is still subscribed once.
Rule and first browser subscribe race for the same symbol (see AC 7): exactly one upstream subscribe.
Last browser leaves while a rule is concurrently adding the same symbol to the watchlist: no unsubscribe is sent.
Browser unsubscribes from a symbol that is both browser-held and watched, then resubscribes: no traffic either time.
Concurrent POSTs for different new symbols at cap-1: exactly one succeeds. Concurrent POSTs for the same new symbol: both succeed (201), one watchlist row, one subscribe.
Rule insert fails after the watchlist insert in the same transaction: both roll back.
Commit succeeds but the response/in-memory update path fails or the process dies: Postgres is truth; startup load restores watchlist and rules.
Multiple rules fire on the same tick: one alert per rule.
Deleted rule whose edge state remains: no alert for deleted rules (existing engine behaviour); alerts for it remain listable.
Alert queue full, DB down mid-run, worker insert error: ingestion and broadcast continue; only warning/error logs with exception type.
GET /api/alerts with empty table returns []; limit exactly 1 and 500 accepted.
Frontend: unmount during in-flight fetch must not set state or throw; error then successful Refresh recovers.
No Finnhub API key (factory returns None): rule creation still works and does not error when upstream is None.

risks.risk: Subscribe/unsubscribe coordination between the watchlist (rule path) and SubscriptionManager (which awaits upstream inside its lock): a naive "skip if in watchlist" in the browser callback can produce zero subscribes when a rule and a browser race, or a wrong unsubscribe. Needs the deterministic interleaving test in AC 7.
Accidentally awaiting Postgres or a lock on the tick path would violate the non-blocking invariant; enqueue must be synchronous put_nowait.

Race-safe cap check: a plain COUNT then INSERT is not safe; needs a lock inside the transaction. The real-PG concurrency test could be flaky if written with sleeps; use asyncio.gather of two requests.
Adding an on-mount fetch to Dashboard may break the existing Dashboard frontend test (unmocked fetch for /api/alerts).
Removing X2 methods changes test_connection_manager.py; coverage of drop-failed-connection behaviour must be preserved via send_to.
Startup backfill of watchlist might exceed the cap for installs with many pre-existing rule symbols; accepted (cap applies only to new symbols).
CLAUDE.md describes a different target (e.g. /api/watchlist, fail-loud startup); this task follows current code and the request, and orchestrator updates CLAUDE.md afterwards.

dependencies.dep: asyncpg and Postgres 16 (existing); TEST_DATABASE_URL for real-PG tests.
Existing fakes: tests/fakes/fake_finnhub.py (must record subscribe/unsubscribe calls and initial symbol set; extend only if it does not already), tests/fakes/fake_db.py.
Frontend: React, Vite, vitest and testing-library already present; no new packages.

spec.self_critique: Every story maps to criteria: story 1 to AC 3,6,7,8; 2 to AC 8-10; 3 to AC 11-14,17-18; 4 to AC 13; 5 to AC 4; 6 to AC 15. All criteria have an observable check. The biggest uncertainty is the exact interleaving behaviour in AC 7 and the unverified shape of FakeFinnhubClient (I did not read it, as instructed only to read named files; the implementer must confirm it records subscribe/unsubscribe and the initial get_symbols set). Second: the startup backfill (AC 10) is an assumption beyond the request text; if the user does not want it, drop AC 10 only. Request acceptance 3-5 and 7 are live checks, covered here by the fast and real-PG tests plus manual verification at the verify stage.
